title: The 10 Best Hand Saws
subtitle: Carpenter saws, Japanese pull saws, flush-cut and coping saws for wood, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A hand saw is still the quickest way to make one cut without dragging out a power tool. We ranked 10 best-sellers from IRWIN, SUIZAN, JORGENSEN and value brands on rating, review volume and features (triple-ground teeth, double-edge blades and replaceable blades). The list mixes push-stroke Western saws for lumber with Japanese pull saws for joinery and flush trimming, plus a coping saw for curves, from about $9 to $43.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: IRWIN Hand Saw, Coarse Cut, ProTouch Handle, 15-Inch (2011201)
products.verdict: IRWIN's 15-inch coarse-cut carpenter saw with Tri-Ground teeth, deep gullets and a thick, rigid blade. It's a classic Western push-stroke saw for cutting lumber to length.
products.best_for: Framing, decking and cutting 2x lumber to length.
products.skip_if: You need fine, splinter-free cuts in trim or hardwood; coarse teeth leave a rough edge.
pros: Tri-Ground teeth and deep gullets clear chips fast
Thick blade stays straight in long cuts
4.8 stars, the highest rating on this page
cons: Tooth count isn't published; IRWIN only calls it coarse cut
No blade guard listed
Push-stroke saws take more effort than a pull saw in fine work

products.name: QYQRQF 14 in. Pro Hand Saw, 11 TPI Fine-Cut Soft-Grip Hardpoint Handsaw
products.verdict: A 14-inch, 11 TPI hardpoint saw that cuts on both strokes. At about $10 it's a cheap general-purpose saw for wood, plastic pipe and wallboard.
products.best_for: A low-cost saw for the garage or truck that handles wood, PVC and drywall.
products.skip_if: You want a saw you can resharpen; hardpoint teeth are used until dull, then the saw is replaced.
pros: Cuts on push and pull strokes
11 TPI leaves a cleaner edge than a coarse framing saw
About 1,000 bought in the past month
cons: 0.9 mm blade is thinner than the HAUTMEC's 1.0 mm
Little-known brand
No blade guard listed

products.name: JORGENSEN 15-Inch Hand Saw, 8 TPI Coarse Blade for Wood Cutting
products.verdict: A 15-inch, 8 TPI rough-cut saw with triple-ground SK5 teeth and a Teflon-coated blade that cuts friction and buildup. A plastic edge protector comes in the box.
products.best_for: Fast rough cuts in framing lumber, posts and yard work.
products.skip_if: You want clean finish cuts; 8 TPI is built for speed, not a smooth edge.
pros: SK5 high-carbon steel blade with Teflon coating
Plastic edge protector included for storage
Triple-ground teeth
cons: 8 TPI leaves a rough edge
Heaviest saw here at 1.35 lb
Fewer reviews than the IRWIN

products.name: RUITOOL Japanese Hand Saw 6 Inch Double Edge Ryoba Pull Saw for Flush Cuts
products.verdict: A 6-inch double-edge Ryoba pull saw: 14 TPI on one edge for softwood and rip cuts, 17 TPI on the other for hardwood and crosscuts. The flexible SK5 blade bends for flush cuts.
products.best_for: Dowels, plugs, small joinery and flush trimming where a big saw won't fit.
products.skip_if: You need to cut through 2x4s or wide boards; a 6-inch blade runs out of reach.
pros: Two tooth patterns on one blade
Flexible enough for flush cuts
6,527 reviews and about 3,000 bought in the past month
cons: 6-inch blade is slow in thick stock
Blade isn't replaceable
Pull saws take some practice if you're used to push saws

products.name: SUIZAN Flush Cut Saw 5" - Japanese Pullsaw Hand Saws Wood Cutting
products.verdict: A made-in-Japan 5-inch flush-cut saw with no-set teeth, so it trims dowels, plugs and tenons flush without scratching the surface. Two edges: 17 TPI and 25 TPI.
products.best_for: Trimming dowels, plugs and edging flush with a finished surface.
products.skip_if: You want a general-purpose saw; this one only does fine trimming.
pros: No-set teeth won't mar the surface around the cut
Thin 0.3 mm blade leaves a narrow kerf
7,211 reviews, the most on this page
cons: Blade is fixed to the handle and not replaceable, per the listing
Too short for anything but trimming

products.name: JORGENSEN 10 Inch Double Edge Japanese Pull Saw with SK5 Blade
products.verdict: A 10-inch double-edge pull saw with induction-hardened SK5 teeth: a coarse 7-12 TPI rip edge and an 18 TPI crosscut edge. The blade swaps out with one screw.
products.best_for: Woodworkers who want one pull saw for both rip cuts and crosscuts in boards.
products.skip_if: You only need a short trim saw; the 6-inch RUITOOL costs less.
pros: Replaceable blade: loosen one screw
Rip and crosscut edges on one blade
Long enough to cut through dimensional lumber
cons: Its 987 reviews are shared with JORGENSEN's 5- and 7-inch pull saws
Plastic handle

products.name: SUIZAN Ryoba Double Edge Saw 9.5" Assembly ver - Japanese Pullsaw Hand Saws
products.verdict: A made-in-Japan 9.5-inch Ryoba with a 9 TPI rip edge and a 15 TPI crosscut edge on a 0.5 mm blade that leaves a 0.8 mm kerf. When the teeth wear, a replacement blade slides in and locks with one screw.
products.best_for: Furniture makers and joiners who want a Japanese-made Ryoba they can re-blade.
products.skip_if: You want the cheapest way into pull saws; it costs about two and a half times the RUITOOL.
pros: Japanese-made blade with a narrow 0.8 mm kerf
Replaceable blade (sold separately)
Hand-wrapped wood handle
cons: Most expensive saw here
323 reviews, far fewer than the smaller SUIZAN

products.name: HAUTMEC 14 Inch Hand Saw for Wood Cutting, 11 TPI Small Crosscut Wood Saw with Triple-Ground Teeth
products.verdict: A 14-inch, 11 TPI crosscut saw with triple-ground teeth and a 1.0 mm blade that resists bending. It's the cheapest full-length saw on this page.
products.best_for: Crosscutting boards, laminate flooring and trim on a tight budget.
products.skip_if: You need fast rough cuts in framing lumber; 11 TPI is slower than an 8 TPI saw.
pros: Lowest price for a full-length saw here
1.0 mm blade, thicker than the QYQRQF's 0.9 mm
Rust-resisting coating
cons: Plastic handle
Can't be resharpened

products.name: GARTOL Hand Saw for Wood Cutting, 2-Piece Japanese Pull Saw Set with 6-Inch Flush Cut Saw and Double-Edged SK5 Blade
products.verdict: Two small Japanese pull saws for about $13: a 6-inch flush-cut saw and a double-edge Ryoba, both with flexible SK5 blades and wooden handles.
products.best_for: Hobby woodworkers who want a flush-cut saw and a small Ryoba for the price of one.
products.skip_if: You want published tooth counts; GARTOL doesn't list TPI for either blade.
pros: Two saws in one box
Flexible SK5 blades for flush cuts
Wooden handles
cons: TPI not listed for either saw
Both blades are short, so it's for small work only

products.name: IRWIN Tools ProTouch Coping Saw (2014400)
products.verdict: IRWIN's coping saw: a flat-bar frame with a 5-1/2 inch throat and a 6-1/2 inch, 17-point high-speed steel blade for tight curves and coped trim joints.
products.best_for: Coping baseboard and crown molding, and cutting curves in thin stock.
products.skip_if: You need straight cuts in boards; a coping saw is for curves.
pros: Cuts tight curves no straight saw can follow
Standard pinned blades are easy to replace
5,227 reviews and about 900 bought in the past month
cons: 5-1/2 in frame depth limits how far from an edge it can cut
Thin blades snap if you twist them

avoid.name: TOLCHENO 20 Inch Pro Hand Saw, 7 TPI 65Mn Steel Ergonomic Non-Slip Handle
avoid.flag: Coarse 7 TPI sold as a fine-cut saw
avoid.verdict: A long, thin-bladed saw whose listing sells its coarsest-on-the-page teeth as fine and precise.
reasons: The listing promises fine, precise cuts from 7 teeth per inch. 7 TPI is a rough-cut tooth, coarser than every saw on this page that publishes a count, and it leaves a ragged edge.
Its 20-inch push-stroke blade is listed at 0.9 mm thick, thinner than the 14-inch HAUTMEC's 1.0 mm. A long, thin blade on a push saw is the one most likely to bend in the cut.
If you want a fast rough-cut saw, the JORGENSEN 15-inch is 8 TPI with an SK5 blade and an edge protector; for fine cuts, the HAUTMEC or QYQRQF 11 TPI saws cost less.

buyers_guide.a: Western saws cut on the push stroke and use a thick blade so it doesn't buckle; they're quick in framing lumber. Japanese pull saws cut on the pull, so the blade can be thin: a narrower kerf, less effort and cleaner cuts. Pick a push saw for 2x lumber and a pull saw for joinery and trim.
Fewer teeth per inch cut faster and rougher: 7 to 8 TPI for framing and yard work, about 11 TPI for general crosscuts in boards and plywood, 15 TPI and up for hardwood, trim and joinery.
A double-edge Japanese pull saw with rip teeth on one edge (for cutting along the grain) and crosscut teeth on the other, so one blade covers both kinds of cut.

buyers_guide.q: What is a flush-cut saw for?
buyers_guide.a: Trimming dowels, plugs and edging level with a surface. Its teeth have no set (they don't bend outward), so the blade can lie flat on the work without scratching it.

buyers_guide.q: Can I sharpen a hand saw?
buyers_guide.a: Most inexpensive saws have hardpoint (induction-hardened) teeth that stay sharp a long time but can't be filed. When they dull, you replace the saw, or just the blade on saws like the JORGENSEN 10-inch and the SUIZAN Ryoba.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a coping saw too?
buyers_guide.a: Only if you cut curves or cope trim joints. Its thin, tensioned blade turns corners no straight saw can follow.
